name: VibeShift Boost – Conversion Engine for WooCommerce
author: Maroun A

sections.description:
VibeShift Boost is a WooCommerce-focused conversion and product-performance plugin designed to help store owners add urgency, social proof, visitor information, countdown campaigns, analytics, and AI-assisted insights to product pages and the WordPress admin dashboard.

Version 3.0.58 hardens public live-visitor endpoints against access to unpublished/password-protected products, bounds live-presence storage, restores the registered read-only live-count endpoint, and adds a versioned Free-to-Pro compatibility status API that reports whether required shared components are loaded and the Free master switch is enabled. It does not validate licenses or expose secrets. Version 3.0.57 corrects the release packaging layout: the SVN trunk and tag contain vibeshift-boost.php and readme.txt directly at their roots, and the installable ZIP folder matches the WordPress.org repository slug. This is a packaging/upgrade-identity correction; it does not migrate or delete store data. Version 3.0.56 removes the obsolete local Pro activation-key form and save endpoint from Free Settings, replaces the unverified disconnected-license warning with neutral VibeShift account-management guidance, and leaves the report recipient blank unless a VibeShift account integration explicitly supplies a valid registered email. Remote trial/license status is not fabricated by the Free plugin. Version 3.0.55 moves the shared-data explanation and reporting filters immediately above the Special Promotions List, adds the Last 6 Hours filter across saved countdown durations, and pre-fills the report recipient from the email supplied by the then-current account mechanism. Version 3.0.54 moves the Customer Location Map to the bottom of the Dashboard and improves daily inventory and print layout. Version 3.0.51 restores the original Product Intelligence / Complete Product Performance heading and single-row search/Add Product toolbar, keeps every matching WooCommerce product card on Products using 100-item query batches, removes the dashboard-only hidden flag and pagination that changed the previous catalog behavior, and keeps the separate Performance Analytics view. Version 3.0.50 separates Overview, Products and Analytics so the full WooCommerce catalog stays on the Products page and analytics uses its own metrics/tables. It also aligns the monthly report CSV to one stable set of columns and avoids classifying a removal using lifetime sales history. Version 3.0.49 includes reports-module security and database-query cleanups. It preserves the existing VibeShift Boost Free features while using a distinctive VibeShift Boost code/data namespace, preserving existing stored data during upgrade, and improving WordPress.org compatibility documentation.

WooCommerce is recommended for the product and storefront features. The plugin is designed to activate without requiring WooCommerce during plugin activation, while WooCommerce-powered features become available when WooCommerce is active.

Features

  • Product countdown campaigns with 6, 10, 15, and 30 day durations, plus a Last 6 Hours remaining-time filter in reports.
  • Optional countdown disabled state (None).
  • Live countdown displayed on the WooCommerce product page.
  • Separate FINAL 6 HOURS countdown when six hours or less remain.
  • Server-side expiration handling that moves an expired product to Draft.
  • Request-time expiration safety fallback in addition to scheduled expiration handling.
  • Dashboard Renew & Reactivate action that republishes a product and starts a fresh countdown.
  • Product Keep action that stops the timer while keeping the product published.
  • Dashboard removal that does not delete the underlying WooCommerce product.
  • Product visitor tracking for real frontend product visits.
  • Today’s product visitor count.
  • Total product visitor information.
  • 30-day visitor information and dashboard analytics where available.
  • Compatibility with existing visitor data stored by older underscore-prefixed meta keys.
  • Product performance list with WooCommerce edit links.
  • Visitor, countdown, AI, conversion, and time-spent dashboard information.
  • Dashboard analytics and conversion-oriented product information.
  • Enable Plugin and Enable Visitors Counter settings switches.
  • Editable visitor counter background and text colors.
  • Editable six-hour warning background and text colors.
  • Centralized Pro account, trial, and license-management links; the Free Settings page does not display or save a Pro activation key.
  • Customer license generation is not included in the plugin; customer license codes are issued separately.
  • Optional AI features that use the site’s configured OpenAI integration when enabled and configured.

External services

VibeShift Boost can optionally connect to OpenAI when the site administrator enables the plugin’s AI features and configures an OpenAI API key. The OpenAI connection is not required for the plugin’s non-AI countdown, visitor, analytics, or WooCommerce features.

When an AI request is made, the plugin sends the product information and aggregated dashboard information needed for the requested analysis, together with the configured AI request settings. Requests are sent only when the administrator has enabled the AI functionality and configured an OpenAI API key.

OpenAI processes the transmitted information under its own terms and privacy policy.

OpenAI Terms of Service: https://openai.com/policies/service-terms/
OpenAI Privacy Policy: https://openai.com/policies/row-privacy-policy/

VibeShift Boost does not provide an OpenAI account and does not pay OpenAI API usage charges.

The plugin also provides ordinary outbound links to the VibeShift UI website for customer accounts, Pro trial information, pricing, and license information. These links do not send site data to VibeShift merely by being displayed.

VibeShift UI: https://vibeshiftui.com/
VibeShift Pro trial: https://vibeshiftui.com/vibe-pro-trial/
VibeShift pricing: https://vibeshiftui.com/vibe-pricing/

Countdown Lifecycle

The countdown system uses a stored start timestamp and one authoritative end timestamp for each active product timer.

  • None disables the countdown and clears its scheduled single expiration event.
  • 6, 10, 15, or 30 Days creates the countdown using one stored start timestamp and one authoritative end timestamp.
  • The WooCommerce frontend reads the stored end timestamp and updates the countdown display every second.
  • When six hours or less remain, the frontend switches to the separate FINAL 6 HOURS countdown state.
  • When the countdown reaches zero, the server-side expiration handler moves the product to Draft.
  • A request-time safety fallback checks for an expired published product so a delayed WP-Cron run does not leave an expired product active indefinitely.
  • Renew & Reactivate republishes the product and creates a fresh countdown.
  • Keep Product stops the countdown while leaving the product published.

WP-Cron timing can be affected by the site’s hosting environment. The request-time safety fallback is therefore used as an additional protection against delayed scheduled tasks.

Visitor Tracking

VibeShift Boost records product visitor activity on the frontend and provides visitor information in the dashboard.

The visitor system is designed to distinguish visitor activity from ordinary page refreshes and to keep daily and longer-term visitor information separate.

The plugin preserves readability of existing visitor information stored by older underscore-prefixed product meta keys so upgrades do not unnecessarily discard previously stored data.

Visitor counts should be interpreted as plugin-recorded visitor activity rather than a guarantee of a unique human identity. Visitor analytics are opt-in: VibeShift Boost does not record product visits until the visitor accepts the first-party analytics consent prompt. The plugin also respects a browser Do Not Track signal.

AI Features

VibeShift Boost includes an optional AI layer for conversion-oriented product analysis and dashboard insights.

When AI is enabled and an OpenAI API key is configured, the plugin can use product and dashboard information to generate AI-assisted conversion insights. The AI system is designed to use the configured model, temperature, and maximum-token settings.

AI output is assistance for store analysis and decision-making. It should be reviewed by the site owner before being treated as a business decision or factual statement.

OpenAI usage may create API costs according to the account and service selected by the site owner. VibeShift Boost does not provide an OpenAI API account.

License and Pro Trial

The Free plugin’s License section connects customers to the official VibeShift UI website for Pro account and license actions.

Customers can use the License section to:

  • Request the 30-day free Pro trial.
  • Sign in to an existing VibeShift customer account.
  • Create a VibeShift customer account.
  • Purchase a Pro license.
  • Manage an existing Pro license through the official VibeShift account and licensing system; the Free plugin does not collect or validate Pro activation keys.

The 30-day trial and customer license are created and managed by the VibeShift website and central licensing service. The Free plugin does not generate customer licenses and does not send customer email addresses to the VibeShift website merely because the License section is displayed.

The Free plugin does not expose a public license-validation endpoint. Pro license activation and validation are handled by the VibeShift Pro licensing system.

Do not place passwords, API secrets, or other private credentials into the license field.

Privacy and Visitor Consent

VibeShift Boost visitor analytics are optional and consent-based. When visitor analytics are enabled, the frontend asks the visitor for permission before recording product visitor activity. A first-party consent cookie remembers the visitor’s choice. The plugin uses product-level visitor counters and date-based visitor history stored in the WordPress database.

Site owners should include VibeShift Boost visitor analytics in their site’s privacy policy and should configure any broader consent-management system required by their jurisdiction or other plugins. VibeShift Boost also respects a browser Do Not Track signal.

The plugin provides privacy-policy guidance through WordPress’s built-in privacy-policy tools.

External Services

VibeShift Boost optionally connects to OpenAI for AI-assisted conversion analysis. This connection is used only when the site owner enables the plugin’s AI features and configures an OpenAI API key.

OpenAI

Service: OpenAI API. It is used to generate optional AI-assisted product and dashboard conversion insights.

Data sent: When an AI analysis is requested, VibeShift Boost sends the product and/or dashboard information selected by the plugin for that analysis, together with the configured AI model and request settings. The plugin sends this data only when AI processing is enabled and an OpenAI API key is available. The OpenAI API key is used for authentication and is not included in the generated analysis content.

Why it is sent: The data is sent to OpenAI so the configured OpenAI model can generate the requested conversion insight, recommendation, forecast, or related AI analysis.

When it is sent: Only when the site owner has enabled AI functionality and the plugin performs an AI request. AI processing is optional; the plugin’s non-AI features do not require OpenAI.

Service website: https://openai.com/
Terms: https://openai.com/policies/service-terms/
Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/row-privacy-policy/

OpenAI usage may create API charges under the site’s OpenAI account. The site owner is responsible for deciding what information is appropriate to send, configuring consent and privacy controls where required, and reviewing OpenAI’s current documentation.

Configuration

After activation, VibeShift Boost provides a single admin area containing the main Version 3 dashboard sections, including:

  • Dashboard
  • Products
  • Analytics
  • Settings

The Settings area provides controls for enabling the plugin, enabling visitor counting, and configuring visitor and final-six-hour warning colors.

Product controls are available from the VibeShift Boost dashboard for supported WooCommerce products.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or newer.
  • PHP 8.0 or newer.
  • WooCommerce recommended for WooCommerce product and storefront features.
  • A working WordPress cron environment is recommended for scheduled countdown expiration handling. The plugin also includes a request-time expiration safety fallback.

Privacy

VibeShift Boost may process product visitor activity and other analytics information needed to provide its dashboard and conversion features.

Site owners are responsible for determining the privacy, cookie, consent, retention, and disclosure requirements that apply to their website and visitors.

If AI features are enabled, information selected by the plugin for AI analysis may be sent to the configured OpenAI service. Site owners should review their own legal, privacy, and data-processing requirements before enabling third-party AI processing.

The plugin does not claim that its visitor tracking is a replacement for a site’s privacy policy, cookie policy, consent-management system, or legal advice.

Support

For support, visit the VibeShift UI website:

https://vibeshiftui.com/

Product information:

https://vibeshiftui.com/vibeshift-boost-conversion-engine-for-woocommerce/

License

VibeShift Boost is licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later.

https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-2.0.html
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  2. Choose Upload Plugin.
  3. Upload the VibeShift Boost ZIP package.
  4. Install the plugin and activate it.
  5. Go to the VibeShift Boost dashboard.
  6. Enable the plugin and configure the visitor counter and display settings as required.
  7. Make sure WooCommerce is active when using WooCommerce product features.
  8. If using AI features, configure the OpenAI integration and enable the relevant AI functionality.
sections.faq:
Is WooCommerce required to activate VibeShift Boost?

No. WooCommerce is recommended for the product and storefront features, but the plugin is designed not to require WooCommerce merely to activate the plugin.

Which countdown durations are available?

The supported product durations are 6, 10, 15, and 30 days. None disables the countdown.

What happens when the countdown reaches zero?

The server-side expiration handler moves the expired product to Draft. A request-time safety fallback provides additional protection if a scheduled WP-Cron task is delayed.

What happens when I use Renew & Reactivate?

The product is republished and a new countdown is started from a fresh start timestamp and authoritative end timestamp.

Does Keep Product delete the product or hide it?

No. Keep Product stops the countdown while keeping the WooCommerce product published.

Does removing a product from the VibeShift dashboard delete the WooCommerce product?

No. Dashboard removal does not delete the underlying WooCommerce product.

Can I use the plugin without visitor counting?

Yes. The visitor counter can be enabled or disabled from Settings.

Does the plugin generate customer license codes?

No. Customer license generation is intentionally not included. License codes are issued separately and entered for activation.

Is AI required?

No. AI functionality is optional and depends on the site’s AI configuration and whether the relevant AI features are enabled.

Does VibeShift Boost guarantee exact human visitor counts?

No analytics plugin can guarantee a perfect count of unique humans under every browser, cache, privacy, bot, and network condition. VibeShift Boost records visitor activity according to its tracking logic and site environment.
sections.changelog:
3.0.58

  • Harden public live visitor endpoints so unpublished, private, password-protected, and missing products do not expose live counts.
  • Restore the registered read-only live-count AJAX endpoint and bound live-presence storage during traffic bursts.
  • Add a versioned, read-only Free-to-Pro compatibility status API. The API does not validate licenses or expose secrets.
  • Preserve existing settings, product metadata, countdowns, visitor history, and report data; no destructive database migration is introduced.

3.0.57

  • Correct release packaging so the SVN trunk and release tag contain the main plugin file and readme.txt directly at their roots.
  • Name the installable ZIP directory to match the WordPress.org repository slug, reducing plugin-basename mismatches on new installs.
  • Preserve existing plugin code, settings, product data, reporting history, and stored options; no database migration or data deletion is introduced.

3.0.55

  • Move report month and promotion filters directly above Special Promotions List, with the shared data-provider note immediately above the list heading.
  • Add a Last 6 Hours filter for active countdowns ending within six hours while retaining each product’s saved campaign duration and single original duration group.
  • Use the currently signed-in WordPress account’s email as the report recipient; leave the field empty if there is no valid account email rather than falling back to the global site administration email.
  • Keep on-screen, CSV, and PDF promotion filtering aligned.

3.0.54

  • Moved Customer Location Map to the bottom of the Dashboard, after AI Insights and management shortcuts.
  • Added a current-day live inventory reading when no end-of-day snapshot has been recorded yet; the UI and exports label it as a live reading. Historic missing snapshots remain blank.
  • Applied the Special Promotions group filter immediately so users can show All groups or one duration at a time.
  • Reworked report print CSS for A4 landscape, full-width tables, controlled wrapping, repeating headers, and multi-page output without horizontal clipping.

3.0.53

  • Complete Customer Geography map powered by WooCommerce billing-country values across all paginated eligible orders.
  • Replaced the grid-only map with a bundled, self-contained Natural Earth world map; countries are shaded only when recorded billing-country data exists.
  • Added an accessible map legend, hover/focus order totals, country summary pills, clear empty/error states, and privacy wording distinguishing country-level aggregates from exact addresses.
  • Cached geography aggregates for 15 minutes and invalidated the cache on WooCommerce order create/update/status/delete/trash events.
  • Preserved Products page rendering, Analytics page rendering, and the existing reporting module.

3.0.52

  • Fixed reports-module PreparedSQL.NotPrepared findings by passing prepared SQL directly to database calls.
  • Added object-cache handling for custom-table existence checks.
  • Documented the uncached one-time migration write: it must execute to preserve ledger records, is idempotent, and never deletes the legacy source table.
  • Preserved the 3.0.51 Products layout, product list, and separate Performance Analytics screen.

3.0.48

  • Addressed latest reports-module Plugin Check findings for translations, binary export output, nonce-validation analysis, and documented module-owned database queries.
  • Retained restored product listings and existing dashboard/product management interface.

3.0.47

  • Removed duplicate product intelligence cards from the Overview dashboard; product cards remain under Products.
  • Added Promotions & Reports admin page with 6/10/15/30-day countdown groups.
  • Added monthly sales/order summary, CSV/PDF export, print view, and emailed PDF with optional CSV.
  • Added an inventory event ledger for new product-removal, stock-update, order-status, and refund events.
  • Historical ending inventory is explicitly unavailable where no snapshot ledger exists; the report does not fabricate historical stock balances.

3.0.35

  • Updated the VibeShift Boost admin branding to use the supplied VibeShift logo in the WordPress menu and dashboard header.
  • Preserved the existing Free functionality and stored data behavior.

3.0.33

  • Replaced the short internal legacy short namespace with a distinctive VibeShift Boost namespace for plugin classes, functions, hooks, options, metadata, AJAX actions, cron hooks, asset handles, and database tables.
  • Added a one-time upgrade migration for existing VibeShift Boost options, post meta, database tables, and scheduled events.
  • Added the WooCommerce dependency declaration for WordPress dependency-aware installations.
  • Removed the dashboard map inline script and moved its data into an HTML data attribute consumed by the enqueued dashboard JavaScript.
  • Removed static inline styling from the license controls.
  • Added the required WordPress.org contributor metadata and clarified external-service documentation.

3.0.30

  • Updated the plugin version to 3.0.30.
  • Connected the Free plugin License section to the official VibeShift customer portal.
  • Added a direct 30-day free Pro trial link.
  • Added direct customer sign-in and account-registration links.
  • Corrected the pricing URL used by the License section.
  • Kept existing Free plugin features and license-key storage behavior unchanged.

3.0.29

  • Removed the Tested up to value from the main plugin header; it is declared only in readme.txt.
  • Documented the optional OpenAI external service, data sent, purpose, conditions, Terms, and Privacy links.
  • Renamed the Settings API sanitizer to sanitize_settings so the registered sanitize callback is explicit and unambiguous to review tooling.
  • Moved the Settings color-field JavaScript from inline dashboard markup into the enqueued admin JavaScript asset.

3.0.27

  • Fixed all reported Plugin Check nonce and slow meta-query warnings.
  • Added WordPress AI Client support with a legacy provider fallback.
  • Added countdown display control for single product pages.
  • Added configurable countdown background and text colors to Settings.
  • Updated storefront visitor and countdown rendering and cache versions.
  • Reworked custom analytics SQL to use WordPress 6.2+ %i identifier placeholders for tables and columns.
  • Removed the unsafe intermediate SQL identifier variables that Plugin Check reported as unescaped.
  • Added short-lived object-cache entries for repeated analytics counts.
  • Reworked uninstall table removal to use $wpdb->prepare() with %i.

3.0.20

  • Repaired analytics identifier handling for Plugin Check compatibility.
  • Removed direct admin-page routing reads from $_GET.
  • Sanitized the product timer form value before comparison.

  • Preserved existing WooCommerce analytics, dashboard, and visitor functionality.

  • Hardened dashboard output handling and analytics database queries.

  • Added consent-based visitor analytics and WordPress privacy-policy guidance.
  • Corrected remaining internationalization domains and strengthened translator guidance.
  • Updated WordPress.org metadata and documentation.

3.0.14

  • Prepared the release for WordPress.org review.
  • Removed the public license-validation REST endpoint and license registry service.
  • Removed the external Leaflet CDN dependency from the admin dashboard.
  • Replaced the map dependency with a local dependency-free order-country visualization.
  • Removed unused direct filesystem storage code.
  • Removed direct debug logging calls.
  • Updated plugin metadata for WordPress 7.1 compatibility metadata.
  • Preserved countdown, visitor, analytics, AI, settings, and account-management behavior without restoring the removed local Pro activation-key form.
  • Improved product-page visitor display and visitor tracking integration.
  • Preserved readability of existing underscore-prefixed visitor meta data.
  • Refined the countdown lifecycle and authoritative timer timestamps.
  • Added independent FINAL 6 HOURS countdown behavior.
  • Added server-side expiration handling and request-time safety fallback.
  • Added Renew & Reactivate and Keep Product lifecycle actions.
  • Refined Settings switches and visitor/final-warning color controls.
  • Kept the license activation field blank on page load.
  • Removed customer-license generation from the plugin package.
  • Excluded old nested ZIP artifacts from the plugin package.

Configuration

After activation, VibeShift Boost provides a single admin area containing the main Version 3 dashboard sections, including:

  • Dashboard
  • Products
  • Analytics
  • Settings

The Settings area provides controls for enabling the plugin, enabling visitor counting, and configuring visitor and final-six-hour warning colors.

Product controls are available from the VibeShift Boost dashboard for supported WooCommerce products.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or newer.
  • PHP 8.0 or newer.
  • WooCommerce recommended for WooCommerce product and storefront features.
  • A working WordPress cron environment is recommended for scheduled countdown expiration handling. The plugin also includes a request-time expiration safety fallback.

Site owners are responsible for determining the privacy, cookie, consent, retention, and disclosure requirements that apply to their website and visitors.

If AI features are enabled, information selected by the plugin for AI analysis may be sent to the configured OpenAI service. Site owners should review their own legal, privacy, and data-processing requirements before enabling third-party AI processing.

The plugin does not claim that its visitor tracking is a replacement for a site’s privacy policy, cookie policy, consent-management system, or legal advice.
